articles.title: Shelly’s new $50 security camera watches your home without a subscription
articles.summary: The high-def camera can livestream to your phone or record events locally to a memory card.
articles.body: After launching a budget-friendly flood sensor last month with impressive battery life, Shelly announced a new $49.99 security camera today that can be used without any additional subscription fees — although that’s still an option if you want to expand its capabilities. The Shelly Camera will be available soon from the company’s online store and other resellers in black or white. Although competitors like Wyze have released 2K security cameras for $40, Shelly’s first camera is limited to 1080P with a wide field of view that stretches 110 degrees horizontally and 70 degrees vertically with night vision capabilities. But there’s no battery, so during installation you’ll also need to route a USB-C cable to deliver power. [Image: Wherever you decide to mount the Shelly Camera you’ll need to be mindful of cable management. When used without a subscription plan the camera can livestream video over Wi-Fi to various devices, capture events locally to a microSD card, and trigger smart home automations through other Shelly devices such as turning on a floodlight when movement is detected. If you do opt to pay for a subscription you’ll gain access to cloud recording as well as smart object detection that can distinguish between people, pets, and vehicles so alerts and automations can be customized for specific scenarios.

articles.title: MasterChef Winner Pankaj Bhadouria shares ‘Cancer’ changed her; says 'I was weakened by infections  that took a massive toll on my physical health'
articles.summary: MasterChef India Season 1 winner Pankaj Bhadouria, who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer, opened up about her ongoing treatment and shared an .
articles.body: MasterChef India Season 1 winner Pankaj Bhadouria, who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer, opened up about her ongoing treatment and shared an emotional update about the challenges she faced during August.Pankaj spoke about her battle with cancer and her second chemotherapy session. She also revealed repeated infections, hair loss and how August took a toll on her physical health. She also mentioned the moments of happiness she experienced with her family and friends.Pankaj took to her social media account and shared a photo from a hospital bed. She wrote, “August turned out to be quite eventful! It started with my second Chemotherapy that hit me really hard. It took a major toll on my health and hair too. Despite all precautions, preventive medicines and care, I was weakened by infections one after the other that took a massive toll on my physical health. And then came the other after effects- the major being hair loss! Believe me, nothing prepares you for it when it actually hits you. Losing my tresses was a shocker that took time coming to terms. But then, as the month moved on came in days that brought in joy and happiness- so many friends from far and near coming to visit me, celebrating festivals. I even snuck in a few sweets!”She added, “And then finally, an evening out with the family after 3 whole months! Yes, we ate out and it felt so good! It felt like a step towards recovery. It’s funny how a word like ‘Cancer’ changes your entire life and that of your family around you too. But then we are learning to live with it in the best way anyone can- with love, support and hope!”Pankaj has been sharing updates about her cancer journey with her followers on social media. Talking about Pankaj Bhadouria's cancer diagnosis, she first publicly revealed her breast cancer diagnosis on May 28, 2026. Sharing a picture from a hospital bed, she wrote, “I have been diagnosed with Breast Cancer. Need your prayers and support.”A day later, she shared that she was going in for surgery and thanked her fans for their love and support. She further revealed that her post-surgery biopsy detected a 2mm invasive HER2-positive component, after which doctors advised chemotherapy and targeted treatment.Before beginning chemotherapy, she had even chosen to cut her long hair short, saying she wanted to enjoy it while she had it.

articles.title: GoPro has been acquired and is getting into ‘defense, government, robotics and aerospace’
articles.summary: GoPro is now aimed at national security and defense, with a new buyer Starman Holdings and a YouTuber investor.
articles.body: GoPro suddenly looks like a very different company than it did just last week. First, YouTuber Mark “Markiplier” Fischbach became the company’s single largest shareholder, without disclosing that in a sponsored review that came out a week later. Now, almost the entire company has been bought by Starman Holding for $285 million in cash, which Starman is characterizing as a “merger.” While GoPro has always been best known as the company that makes consumer action cameras, the press release takes a bit of a different tone: founder and CEO Nick Woodman now calls GoPro “a leading American imaging and optical solutions company, addressing important areas of national security related to cameras, optics and AI infrastructure.” “The combination of GoPro’s world-class optical expertise and intellectual property with Starman’s advanced transceiver capabilities and U.S. manufacturing platform creates a unique opportunity. Together, we intend to bring production of these critical components back to the United States,” reads a quote from Starman Holdings CEO Charles Tebele. What is Starman Holding? According to Tebele’s online bio, it’s got a lot of fingers in a lot of pies — but you might recognize its phone case brands Incipio, Incase, Griffin, and Survivor. It appears that Starman Holding owns Onward Brands, which acquired Vinci Brands, a division of Armor Acquisition, which bought them from Incipio back in 2021. You might also recognize its brand Digital Gadgets, which reportedly donated to NY governor Kathy Hochul’s campaign around the same time it secured $637 million in contracts for COVID-19 tests, then sued the administration over subsequent bids. Amid its financial troubles — it had lost most of its value and had $92 million in debt — GoPro had already announced it would begin defense and aerospace consulting in April. The new press release says GoPro will “continue to fully support its existing consumer products” and grow in consumer, but it sounds a bit like a pivot. I’m just spitballing here, but when I think about tiny cameras, optical transceivers, and defense manufacturing, it reminds me of those long reels of optical fiber that come out the back of attack drones — and how US consumer drones have largely been set aside in favor of war. Starman says shareholders will keep 10 percent of the company’s shares; Markiplier purchased 8.5 percent. It’s not clear if the YouTuber plans to keep them, or will get a rapid payday; the value of the stock doubled overnight, though it’s currently settling down. [Image: The deal should close by the end of the year, according to the press release; it does not yet appear to have hit the SEC’s filing system yet.
